To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of the population is consuming inadequate amounts of fruits and vegetables, and that this inadequacy is associated with the consumption of other food items, such as sweets, soft drinks and fast food, and with demographic characteristics.
The majority of adults in Portugal do not meet the recommendations for fruit and vegetable consumption.
The most important determinant of inadequate fruit and veg intake in Portugal was the lack of knowledge of the recommended daily intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of social capital and social support in the context of fruit and vegetable consumption.
the determinants of fruit and vegetable consumption among Portuguese adults.
the determinants of inadequate fruit intake, inadequate vegetable intake, and inadequate fruit intake plus inadequate vegetable intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the determinants of fruit and vegetable consumption are complex and multifactorial, and that the relationship between fruit and vegetable consumption and health is not linear.
the consumption of fruits and vegetables is beneficial to human health and should be promoted.
the most important determinant of inadequate fruit and vegetables consumption in the Portuguese population is the low frequency of intake of fruits, vegetables and fruit juices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important determinants of insufficient intake of fruits and vegetables among Portuguese adults are: low income, low level of education, low physical activity and smoking habits.

the most important determinants for fruit and vegetable consumption are the availability and accessibility of fruit and vegetables, the social norms and social support, as well as the price of fruit and vegetables.

the most significant determinants of inadequate fruit consumption are the same determinants of inadequate vegetable consumption: being female, being younger, having a lower level of education, being single, and being unemployed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of adults in Portugal are not consuming adequate amounts of fruits and vegetables, and the prevalence of this problem has not decreased over the past 10 years.
the current guidelines of 5 servings of fruits and vegetables per day for adults are too low.
the determinants of inadequate fruit consumption are not the same as the determinants of insufficient vegetable consumption.
